details.description: Studio voices are a Google Cloud Text-to-Speech voice type designed for news reading and broadcast content, and are intended for use with long-form texts such as narration and news reading, per Google's Voice Types and release-note documentation. They reached general availability in February 2024. Google's Voices list documents Studio voices for English (UK), English (US), and French (France), with named voices such as en-GB-Studio-B and fr-FR-Studio-A; a related Studio multispeaker voice type for discussions and interviews remains experimental.
advantages: Reached general availability (GA) as a voice type purpose-built for news reading and broadcast content, per Google's Voice Types documentation and February 2024 release notes.
Designed specifically for long-form texts such as narration and news reading, per Google's Text-to-Speech release notes.
Supports SSML markup for controlling speech output, per Google's Voice Types documentation.
disadvantages: Documented for only three languages/locales (English UK, English US, and French France), per Google's Voices documentation, far fewer than Google's Standard or WaveNet voice types.
Does not support the <mark>, <emphasis>, <prosody pitch>, or <lang> SSML tags that other voice types allow, per Google's Voice Types documentation.
use_cases: News reading and broadcast-style content, per Google's Voice Types documentation.
Long-form narration, per Google's Text-to-Speech release notes.

sources.title: Supported voices and languages | Cloud Text-to-Speech Documentation

notes: This catalog entry (google_speech/studio) covers the single-speaker Studio voice type as a group, not one named voice; the separate Studio multispeaker type is still experimental per Google's docs and is not what this entry describes. Catalog facts carry no deprecation_date, and no deprecation is documented.
